name: Syndrome of Reduced Sensitivity to Thyroid Hormone

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Resistance to Thyroid Hormone

criteria.description: Elevated circulating free T4 and/or free T3 levels with non-suppressed or elevated TSH
Presence of variable clinical features of thyroid hormone excess or deficiency in different tissues
Identification of pathogenic variants in the THRB gene
Exclusion of other causes of elevated thyroid hormones such as TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated thyroid hormones with non-suppressed TSH plus either clinical features consistent with thyroid hormone resistance or genetic confirmation of THRB mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended for confirmation; differential diagnosis includes TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma and assay interference.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated serum free thyroxine with non-suppressed TSH
searchTerms: high thyroid hormone with normal TSH
thyroid hormone imbalance with normal TSH

pathognomonic.notes: Manifested as mixed signs of hypo- and hyperthyroidism
Pathogenic variants in thyroid hormone receptor beta gene
searchTerms: mutation in thyroid hormone receptor gene
THRB gene alteration affecting thyroid function

occasional.notes: Sensorineural hearing loss reported in some cases

rare.notes: Rare but potentially serious cardiac rhythm disturbances
Rare reports of eye movement disorders
Skeletal maturation delay in some patients

laboratory: Elevated free T4 and free T3 with non-suppressed or elevated TSH
imaging: Thyroid ultrasound showing goiter or nodules
Pituitary MRI to exclude TSH-secreting adenoma
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the THRB gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Neuropsychological testing for attention and cognitive deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated TSH with elevated thyroid hormones
Elevated total thyroid hormones with normal free hormone levels

redFlags: Persistent elevated thyroid hormones with non-suppressed TSH
Signs of both hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism in the same patient
Family history of thyroid hormone resistance or THRB mutations
references: Refetoff S, et al. Resistance to thyroid hormone: genetic basis and clinical implications. Endocr Rev. 2014.
Mullur R, et al. Thyroid hormone resistance syndrome: clinical and molecular aspects. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2017.
Orphanet: Syndrome of reduced sensitivity to thyroid hormone, ORPHA:596426.
